title: India Tells Its Nationals in Saudi Arabia: Stay Indoors During Aerial Attacks
excerpt: The Embassy of India in Riyadh issued a fresh safety advisory on October 15 after two days of Houthi attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities; its helplines are open round the clock.
body:
• The Embassy of India in Riyadh advised Indians in Saudi Arabia on October 15 to stay indoors in case of an aerial attack, keep away from windows, and follow Saudi local authorities.
  • Help is available round the clock: toll-free 800-244-0003, WhatsApp +966-543929706, and email cw.riyadh@mea.gov.in.
  • The advisory follows two days of Houthi attacks, including an October 13 fire at a Yanbu oil facility that killed an Indian worker and an October 14 missile strike on Abha airport that killed a passenger.
  • Air travel is already disrupted: Indian airlines have cancelled Saudi flights through October 17 and a 24-hour control room is helping Umrah pilgrims.

India has told its nationals in Saudi Arabia to stay indoors in case of an aerial attack, in a fresh advisory issued by the Embassy of India in Riyadh on October 15 after two days of Houthi strikes on Saudi airports and energy facilities. The advisory, reported by NDTV, asks community members to remain inside during any attack, stay away from windows, and follow the instructions of Saudi local authorities.

The embassy's community welfare wing can be reached on the toll-free number 800-244-0003, on WhatsApp at +966-543929706, and by email at cw.riyadh@mea.gov.in. Indians in the kingdom form its largest expatriate community, and the embassy maintains a dedicated community welfare channel for emergencies of this kind.

Two Days of Attacks Behind the Advisory

The warning follows a sharp escalation. On October 13, a fire at an oil facility in Yanbu, on the Red Sea coast, killed an Indian worker who was working as a firefighter, according to Arab News; the Houthis claimed an attack on the site, a claim Saudi authorities have not confirmed, and the cause of the fire remains under investigation. On October 14, a missile strike on Abha International Airport in the south killed a passenger, and flights from the airport were suspended.

https://x.com/IndiaToday/status/2110394826982379673

Those attacks land on top of a fortnight of disruption that has already stranded travellers. Riyadh's airport has faced repeated closures, and Indian airlines have cancelled Saudi flights through October 17. India has also opened a 24-hour control room to help Umrah pilgrims caught by the cancellations.

What Indians in Saudi Should Do Now

The guidance is specific and worth saving before it is needed. During any aerial attack alert: stay indoors, move away from windows, and follow Saudi civil defence and local authority instructions rather than social media reports. Keep the embassy's toll-free number and WhatsApp line stored in your phone, and make sure family members in India have them too. Travellers booked on Saudi routes in the next several days should check flight status with their airline before leaving for the airport, as suspensions have been extended at short notice throughout this escalation.

There is no evacuation advisory, and the embassy has not asked Indians to leave the kingdom. The message is narrower and more practical: the threat is real enough that the mission wants every Indian household in Saudi Arabia to know exactly what to do in the minutes an alert sounds.
